questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was close the Denmark, the university had a great academic profile and offered some courses that were different from the ones I could choose at UCPH. Moreover, I had an opportunity to improve my German.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. In the beginning I had some troubles finding information about the courses, but has soon as I got familiar with the website, it was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was in contact with the global office at the university and the faculty before the study period, and they were very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The was only one zoom-session, and it was right before the study-period started. I didn't learn anything new, and received any information that wasn't available on their website.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing on wg-gesucht, which was easy. I also know that there are many other student-houses easily available off campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive, but it is also a good opportunity to meet young local people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university offers a lot of housing, but I was too late with the application so I didn't receive any. So I really recommend keeping an eye on your email. With that student housing you also get to live with the other exchange students, and it is way cheaper (200-300 euros)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is pdf-document that you have to fill out, and send to an email. Very weird.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration was very frustrating. In general, you do not register for the course, but only for the exam - and the deadline for the exam is very close to the actual exam date. With this procedure, you are able to try out a lot of different courses before you sign-up for it which is nice. But it is also very annoying, as you need the "pre-approval" from the back home and also need to make the learning agreement. And furthermore, a lot of courses had limited spaces. So in the end, two week after the semester started I knew which courses I was registred for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Information on the website and one student assistant working at the international office at the faculty.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Luckily, I got all the courses I wanted and three of them even had limited participants.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to the first lectures before signing-up. The procedure can be quite frustrating, but just take it easy and do not stress to much about it - it will all work out in the end :)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I could choose courses from the whole faculty, there was a lot of very interesting courses and seminars that I could choose from.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say the teaching-level is quite high, at least on the same level as at UCPH. But the exams are easier. I also had seminar, which was a little complicated for me as the format was very different from the seminars that I knew from UCPH. So, I spend a lot of time studying for it but at the same time I also learned a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The teaching is not as interactive between the students and teacher as in Copenhagen. And some of the courses also didn't really have any particular readings. 
In a lot of the courses you also have to do a presentation, which accounts for percentage of the final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Macroeconomics 
Monetary Theory and Policy
Wealth and Income Distribution 
Causal Inference in Economics: Methods and Application in Empirical Political Economy 
Topics in Growth Theory (Seminar)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend "causal inference in economics" and "monetary theory and policy". Both really cool courses, and I learned a lot. Especially in the first one, which was an econometric course but explained in a very practical way, which made it easy to understand. I am sure I will use a lot from the course in the future.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I paid a Semesterbeitrag, which is mandatory at most German universities. At Goethe uni, it was 376 euros for one semester. But it also covers all public transportion within Frankfurt and a large area around the city. Therefore the local transportion I have listed is only for the bike that I rented while I was there.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Going out to eat, groceries and the food at campus was way less expensive than I expected. 
I didn't expect to spend so much on housing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different sports, events, a semester-party. The student-card also gave access to the botanical garden. The university definitely had an amazing campus-life, which is what I am going to miss the most.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any sports myself as it didn't fit my schedule, but I heard a lot of good things about it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I definitely recommend visiting the cities and small towns located around Frankfurt, like Wiesbaden, Heidelberg, Marburg, Cologne. I also recommend to go on some hikes, as there is some amazing nature and places close by.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I didn't find it difficult at all. The only thing I had to adjust to is that all stores and supermarkets are closed on Sundays in Germany ;)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: As all my courses was only offered to mainly two master-degrees, which are both very small with about 40 students per year and have a lot of other international students, I easily got to talk with the local students. But, I think I would just recommend to start a conversation yourself. I found that everyone is very open to meet new people. And, in general, Frankfurt is a very international city.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It is not so much of a cultural difference, but I found it challenging that people working in stores, restaurants and health care do not speak english very well.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really like that Germany is such a diverse society, with influences from many different cultures. And at the same time, I also really appreciate the German culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get a bike, use the facilities of the university (the libraries are amazing), and participate in the German course before the lecture period starts. I gives you an opportunity to meet other exchange students, get to know the University and settle before the lectures starts.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not anything I haven't mentioned before.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It is all the people that I got to meet from around the world, and just all the different perspectives on the world that I learned.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge for me was that I was the only danish person among the other exchange students at the university. It would have been have nice to have someone, where you share the same references and background.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
